summary: Asks Hosts to warn their users when the local IMP announces it is going down. BBN Report 1822 defines an IMP-to-Host message that says when the IMP will go down, for how long and why, but Hosts were not reliably passing that on to people using the network.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC asks Hosts to tell users when the local IMP reports that it is going down. The author says logging the message on a teletype is not enough.

subtitle: A request for Hosts to notify users about an impending local IMP outage.

tldr.problem: Users were not generally warned when their local IMP sent a message that it was going down.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC urges Hosts to relay the IMP Going Down message to network and local network users instead of only logging it.
tldr.outcome: The note also reminds readers that Tuesday mornings are reserved for network software maintenance.

facts.label: Maintenance window
facts.value: Tuesday, 7 a.m. to 9 a.m. Eastern Time

sections.title: The IMP Going Down Message
sections.content: BBN Report 1822 defines IMP-to-Host message type 2 as the IMP Going Down message. It tells the Host when the local IMP will go down, for how long, and why.
sections.plainLanguage: The IMP sends its Host a message about an upcoming shutdown. The message includes when it will happen, how long it will last, and why.

sections.title: Hosts Should Warn Their Users
sections.content:
The RFC says users will not generally be forewarned unless the Host sends them a message. It urges Hosts to warn both network users and local users of the network when they receive the IMP Going Down message.

The author says merely logging the received message on a teletype, as many Hosts did, seems insufficient.
sections.plainLanguage: Hosts should pass the outage warning on to their users. Simply recording it on a teletype does not reliably warn people.

sections.title: Network Software Maintenance Window
sections.content: The RFC reminds readers that Tuesday mornings from 7 a.m. to 9 a.m. Eastern Time are reserved for Network Software Maintenance, as announced in RFC 440.
sections.plainLanguage: The notice reminds readers of a regular network software maintenance window. It is Tuesday from 7 to 9 a.m. Eastern Time.
